answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer: No, increasing to 80 miles would overtax recovery and raise injury risk.

new.analysis:
The week follows the build pattern: 5–6 easy runs, one quality session, a long run, and two rest days. The volume stays near 40–42 miles, matching the previous week’s 40.01 miles, so no shock. The quality session is kept to one day (Wednesday) to avoid back‑to‑back hard work. The long run is 16 mi, 5 % longer than the 15 mi from last week, still at an easy pace to build endurance without adding high‑intensity stress.

The plan keeps heart‑rate zones 1–2 high (≈ 75 %) and limits hard time to the single Wednesday workout. Recovery days are Monday and Friday; Saturday is a very light easy run to loosen the legs. This structure supports the build phase while preserving the 80 % easy‑run target.

Answering the question: increasing to 80 mi would overload recovery and could cause injury, so it is not recommended.
